Inglewood, California
  October 6, 2020

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on
Tuesday, October 6, 2020, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:01 p.m.
The Acting City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Franklin, and;
  Absent:  None.
City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Aisha Thompson  Acting City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEM. Mayor
Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City
Council on Closed Session Item No. CS-1.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:01 p.m. for Closed Session
Item Nos. CS-1.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called
the City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing
Authority at the hour of 2:05 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary
announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Authority  Chairman  Butts,  Council
  Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and
  Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.

as follows:

  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Jacquelyn Gordon  Staff Assistant

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority

Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons
present who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing
Authority on any item on the Agendas.

Gil Mathieu, District 4, spoke regarding Agenda Items Nos. 4, 6, 7, 8, and the
Warrant Registrar.

 142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member

  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority

  Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 301  PUBLIC HEARING NOT HELD – SHORT TERM RENTAL
  REGULATIONS AND SHORT TERM RENTAL FEES. The public hearing
  was tabled to October 27, 2020 at 2:00 p.m.

 183  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – AN APPEAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION
  RESOLUTION NO. 1853, DENYING SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2019-
  014 (SP 2019-014) TO ALLOW THE SALE OF BEER AND WINE FOR
  OFF-SITE CONSUMPTION WITHIN AN EXISTING CONVENIENCE
  MARKET AT 400 W. MANCHESTER BOULEVARD UPHELD. The Acting
  City Clerk announced the next scheduled matter was a public hearing to appeal
  Planning Commission Resolution No. 1853, denying Special Use Permit No.
  2019-014 (SP 2019-014) to allow the sale of beer and wine for off-site
  consumption within an existing convenience market at 400 W. Manchester
  Boulevard, that notice was given in the time, form and manner as required by law,
  and no communications were received.

  Artie Fields, City Manager, presented the staff report dated October 6, 2020.

  Mindy Wilcox, Planning Manager, gave a brief oral report.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the
  City Council on this matter.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4 resident, commented he is in favor of granting the
  applicant the special use permit.

  Speaker (Name Unknown), Business owner at 400 West Manchester Blvd.,
  commented she is in favor of request because the special use permit will help out
  the other businesses in the area.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comments portion at the hour of 2:15 p.m.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded
  by Mayor Butts that the City Council does hereby: 1) Overturn the Planning
  Commission’s decision; and 2) Approve and grant the special use permit (SP
  2019-014) but prohibiting the sale of alcohol in single cans. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  PROCLAMATION RECOGNIZING OCTOBER 7, 2020 AS CLEAN AIR
  DAY. Mayor Butts read the proclamation recognizing October 7, 2020 as Clean
  Air Day.

  Chris Chavez, Deputy Policy Director for the Coalition for Clean Air thanked the
  City Council for the proclamation and the City Council’s continued support.
